pk/math.text: Recites numbers up to 20 in sequence.
Recognizes numerals and uses counting as part of play and as a means for determining quantity.
Matches numerals to sets of objects with the same number, 0-10.
Describes sets as having more, less, same as/equal.
Quickly recognizes and names how many items are in a set up to four items.
Tells numbers that come before and after a given number up to 10.
Matches two equal sets using one-to-one correspondence and understands they are the same.
Counts at least 10 objects using one-to-one correspondence.
Practices combining, separating, and naming quantities.
Describes data from classroom graphs using numerical math language.
With adult guidance and when counting, understands and can respond with the last number counted to represent quantity (cardinality).
Uses mathematical terms to describe experiences involving measurement.
Compares objects using two or more attributes, such as length, weight, and size.
Uses a variety of techniques and standard and nonstandard tools to measure and compare length, volume (capacity) and weight.
Associates and describes the passage of time with actual events.
Independently orders objects using one characteristic and describes the criteria used.
Sorts and classifies objects using one or more attributes or relationships.
Creates and extends simple, repeating patterns.
Uses appropriate directional language to indicate where things are in their environment: positions, distances, order.
Uses deliberate manipulation and describes process for fitting objects together.
Recognizes and names common two-dimensional and three-dimensional shapes, their parts, and attributes.
Combines simple shapes to form new shapes.
Estimates using mathematical terms and understands how to check the estimate.
Uses simple strategies to solve mathematical problems and communicates how he/she solved it.
Uses reasoning skills to determine the solution to a mathematical problem and communicates why.

pk/language.text: Listens and responds on topic to conversations and group discussions for an extended period.
Listens to and follows multi-step directions.
Extends/expands thoughts or ideas expressed.
Demonstrates understanding of more complex vocabulary through everyday conversations.
Connects new vocabulary from activities, stories, and/or books with prior experiences and conversations.
Uses more complex gestures and actions to enhance verbal communication of needs and wants.
Communicates feelings using appropriate non-verbal gestures, body language, and actions.
Uses spoken language that can be understood with ease.
Demonstrates use of expanded sentences and sentence structures to ask questions and/or respond verbally.
Describes activities, experiences, and stories with more detail.
Uses new and expanded vocabulary in a variety of situations.
Prior to reading, uses prior knowledge, story title, and pictures to make predictions about story content.
Retells familiar stories.
Discusses books or stories read aloud and can identify characters and setting in a story.
Makes real-world connections between stories and real-life experiences.
Develops an alternate ending for a story.
Listens and differentiates between sounds that are the same and different.
Identifies and produces rhyming words.
Isolates the initial (beginning) sounds in words with adult guidance.
Segments sentences into individual words.
Segments words into syllables.
Manipulates and blends sounds (phonemes) with adult guidance.
With prompting and support, recognizes and names some upper and lower case letters of the alphabet.
Demonstrates interest in different kinds of literature, such as fiction books, non-fiction books, and poetry, on a range of topics.
Understands that letters form words. Understands that words are separated by spaces in print.
With prompting and support, tracks words from left to right, top to bottom, and page to page.
Recognizes and reads environmental print.
Identifies the front, back, top, and bottom of a book. Points to the title of familiar books or stories and where to begin reading a story.
Draws pictures and copies letters and/or numbers to communicate.
Uses writing tools.
Uses writing for a variety of purposes.
Writes some letters of the alphabet.

pk/science.text: Uses senses to observe, classify, and learn about objects and environment.
Uses simple tools correctly to experiment, observe, and increase understanding.
Records observations through dictating to an adult and drawing pictures or using other forms of writing.
Experiments, compares, and formulates hypotheses related to scientific properties.
Describes properties of water, including changes to the states of water.
Explores and begins to describe properties of rocks, soil, sand, and mud.
Makes simple observations of the characteristics, movement, and seasonal changes of sun, moon, stars, and clouds. Compares the day time/night time cycle.
Uses appropriate vocabulary to discuss climate and changes in weather.
Observes, explores and describes a variety of animals and plants. Describes their basic needs and life cycles of living things.
Discriminates between living and non-living things.
Identifies and describes the functions of many body parts.
Explores and describes position and movement of objects and toys.
Investigates and describes different types or speeds of motion.
Describes materials by their physical properties and states of matter.
Uses classroom objects to function as simple machines to enhance child directed play.
Understands that people have an impact on the environment and participates in efforts to protect the environment.

pk/social.text: Identifies self as a unique member of a specific group or demographic that fits into a larger world picture.
Identifies personal characteristics, preferences, thoughts, and feelings.
Shows confidence in a range of abilities and the capacity to accomplish tasks and take on new tasks.
Shows independence in his/her own choices.
Effectively uses words, sentences, and actions to communicate needs, ideas, opinions, and preferences.
With adult guidance, uses verbal and non-verbal expressions to describe and explain a full range of emotions.
Uses pretend play to present emotions of self and others.
With adult guidance, distinguishes between positive and negative emotions and the conditions that evoke each.
Independently follows rules and routines.
Regulates own emotions and behaviors and seeks out adult support when needed.
Regulates a range of impulses.
Manages transitions and adapts to changes in schedules and routines independently.
Transitions well into new, unfamiliar settings.
Uses a familiar adult’s suggestions to decide how to respond to a specific situation.
Shows affection to familiar adults by using more complex words and actions.
Seeks out adults as a resource for help and assistance.
Develops and maintains friendships with other children.
Plays cooperatively with a few peers for a sustained period of time.
Attempts to resolve conflicts using appropriate strategies.
Shows emerging empathy and understanding of peers by attempting to comfort and help.
Shows respect for peers’ personal space and belongings.
Takes initiative to learn new concepts and tries new experiences. Initiates and completes new tasks by himself/herself.
Selects and carries out activities without adult prompting.
Sets goals and develops and follows through on plans.
Demonstrates eagerness to learn about and discuss new topics, ideas and tasks.
Asks questions and seeks new information. With assistance, looks for new information and wants to know more.
Increasingly seeks out and explores unfamiliar objects in the environment.
Engages in independent activities and continues tasks over a period of time.
Practices to improve skills that have been accomplished.
Works cooperatively with others to successfully achieve a goal or accomplish a task.
Persists in trying to complete a task after previous attempts have failed.
Engages in elaborate and sustained imagined play and can distinguish between real life and fantasy.
Willingly joins in sustained cooperative play and learning with others to complete a task.
Demonstrates flexibility in taking on various roles in a group setting.
Demonstrates inventiveness, imagination, and creativity to solve a problem.
Considers a variety of possible solutions and exhibits flexibility if an alternate approach is suggested by a peer or an adult.
Recovers quickly from setbacks and differences in opinion in a group setting.
Describes his/her family structure and family roles.
Describes similarities and differences between self and others.
Identifies and follows rules of the classroom community and displays competence at engaging in appropriate social behavior.
Explains diverse customs and cultural celebrations within the home, classroom and community.
Recognizes similarities and differences between own cultures and that of others.
Creates simple representations of home, school, and community.
Identifies and describes aspects of his/her community.
Completes jobs to contribute to his/her community and communicates why it is important.
Describes the roles and responsibilities of a variety of occupations.
Describes how people interact economically and how goods and services are exchanged.
Explores the uses of technology and understands its role in the environment.
Recognizes and describes sequence of events with accuracy.
Differentiates between past, present, and future.

Uses appropriate vocabulary to discuss climate and changes in weather.

Investigates and describes different types or speeds of motion.

Uses classroom objects to function as simple machines to enhance child directed play.
Understands that people have an impact on the environment and participates in efforts to protect the environment.
